datasets.title: Palestine - Geodata of Damage Assessment in Jarara Area, Gaza Strip - Occupied Palestinian Territory
datasets.description: This map illustrates satellite-detected damage and destruction in the Jarara area, Gaza Strip, resulting from the July/August 2014 violence in the area. Using a satellite image collected 01 August 2014 by the Pleiades satellite, and compared with a pre-crisis Pleiades image collected 6 July 2014, UNOSAT analysis has identified 1,369 damaged structures, including 575 destroyed structures, 233 severely damaged structures and 561 moderately damaged structures. In addition, 182 craters on roads and in agricultural and non-urbanized areas are also visible as of 01 August 2014. This is a preliminary analysis and has not yet been validated in the field. Please send ground feedback to UNITAR/UNOSAT.. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/geodata-of-damage-assessment-in-jarara-area-gaza-strip-occupied-palestinian-t-august-07-2014]
datasets.details: This is a preliminary assessment and has not yet been validated in the field. It is important to consider the characteristics of the source imagery used in the analyses when interpreting results. For damage assessments it should be noted that only significant damage to the structural integrity of the buildings analyzed can be seen in imagery, while minor damage such as cracks or holes may not be visible at all. For flood extractions using radar data it is important to note that urban areas and highly vegetated areas may mask the flood signature and result in underestimation of flood waters. Users with specific questions or concerns should contact unosat@unitar.org to seek clarification.

lineage.description: UNOSAT analysts compared pre-crisis Pleiades satellite imagery (6 July 2014) with post-event imagery (1 August 2014) to detect and classify damage in the Jarara area. Damage was categorized into destroyed, severely damaged, and moderately damaged structures, plus road/agricultural craters, resulting in a spatial geodatabase of 1,369 damaged structures and 182 craters.

sources.name: United Nations Satellite Centre (UNOSAT)
sources.description: Satellite-detected damage assessment using multi-temporal Pleiades imagery comparison (pre-crisis 6 July 2014 vs. post-event 1 August 2014) to identify and classify damaged structures and infrastructure damage in the Jarara area.
